name: Meropenem
summary: Broadest-spectrum beta-lactam; stable to most beta-lactamases including ESBLs and AmpC — definitive therapy for severe resistant infections.
mechanism: Carbapenem beta-lactam that inhibits penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs); stable to most beta-lactamases, including ESBLs and AmpC cephalosporinases.

dosing.adult: 1 g IV every 8 hours (500 mg-2 g every 8 hours depending on indication)

safety.lactation: Compatible — minimal excretion in breast milk
warnings: Seizures (higher risk with renal impairment/CNS disease — though lower than imipenem)

clinicalPearls: Carbapenem of choice when ESBLs are suspected; lower seizure risk than imipenem
No activity against MRSA, VRE, or Stenotrophomonas — not a monotherapy panacea
good: The broadest beta-lactam — definitive therapy for ESBL and severe mixed infections.
bad: Carbapenem resistance pressure — reserve appropriately; C. difficile and seizure risk.

provenance.notes: Curated from standard infectious-disease/pharmacology references. Values omitted where not confidently known — nothing invented.
